issue_context.title: It seems that SamplingParams doesnt support the bad_words_ids parameter when generating
issue_context.body:
`bad_words_ids` described [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/generation/configuration_utils.py#L145C11-L145C11) is useful for production applications.
However It seems that vlllm doesnt support the bad_words_ids parameter when generating.
Is there a plan to support it?
```
  bad_words_ids(`List[List[int]]`, *optional*):
  List of list of token ids that are not allowed to be generated. Check
  [`~generation.NoBadWordsLogitsProcessor`] for further documentation and examples.
```
comments: I hope this can be a possible bad_words_ids stuff implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/5986.

review_comments: I wanted to specify the type of the tokenizer here. But found out (during PR auto code checks) that... `MistralTokenizer` has a different `encode`'s signature, so I had to add a tokenizer class check below to handle Mistral's case differently...
Let's import this from `vllm.sampling_params` instead of copying the definition.

It is not copied, it is just moved from `vllm.sampling_params` to this file. Is it Ok?

It seemed more logical to me to place this `LogitsProcessor` in a file near the newly introduced `NoBadWordsLogitsProcessor` (all these "base" logits processors in one place).
I see what you mean now. That's fine then.
Since the original PR has faded into history, I want to bring to the surface one of the notes which I believe might be important (at least to the point where it's worth highlighting it again)

This differs from the original inequality here: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/generation/logits_process.py#L1131
```python
if len(sequence_ids) > input_ids.shape[1]:  # the sequence is longer than the context, ignore
    continue
```

I may be wrong, but it seemed we should allow for one token to be generated (so + 1).
According to your interpretation, we should also change `prefix_length` to `len(bad_word_ids)`. See if your tests still pass with this change.

One passes, one fails: Well, I think, I better try come up with some illustration of the idea (to make the picture clearer for everybody, including me :slightly_smiling_face:) Suppose, `past_tokens_ids = ["bye"]` (well, that's not ids, but words — let's go with it for simplicity). And `bad_word_ids = ["bye", "world"]`. So, we do not want "bye world" to be generated, but we already have "bye" generated. What is happening now: ```python past_tokens_ids = ["bye"] bad_word_ids = ["bye", "world"] if len(bad_word_ids) > len(past_tokens_ids) + 1: # 2 > 1 + 1 -> False # so we are not skipping `bad_word_ids` continue prefix_length = len(bad_word_ids) - 1 # 2 - 1 = 1 last_token_id = bad_word_ids[-1] # "world" actual_prefix = past_tokens_ids[-prefix_length:] # ["bye"] expected_prefix = bad_word_ids[:prefix_length] # ["bye"] assert len(actual_prefix) == len(expected_prefix) # 1 == 1 is_match = tuple(actual_prefix) == tuple(expected_prefix) # ["bye"] == ["bye"] last_token_bias[last_token_id] += ( self._SMALLEST_LOGIT if is_match else self._NEUTRAL_LOGIT) # "world" gets float("-inf") as logit ``` So, the word "world" is prohibited.
I see, thanks for the detailed explanation.
